examples.ko: 옛날에 그 나라를 정복한 왕이 있었어요.
examples.en: Long ago there was a king who conquered that country.
His dream is to conquer Mount Everest.

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 드디어 이 지역 시장을 정복했어요.
examples.en: Our team finally conquered the market in this region.
I study every day to conquer the difficult exam.

examples.ko: 그 왕은 넓은 땅을 정복하고 큰 제국을 세웠어요.
examples.en: The king conquered vast lands and built a great empire.

examples.ko: 이 게임의 마지막 단계를 정복하기가 정말 어려워요.
examples.en: It is really hard to conquer the last stage of this game.

explain: 힘으로 땅이나 나라를 차지할 때도 쓰고, 산이나 어려운 시험을 끝까지 해냈다는 비유로도 많이 써요. '이기다'는 경기나 싸움의 결과에 쓰고, '정복하다'는 대상을 완전히 내 것으로 만든다는 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: It is used for taking over land or a country by force, and also figuratively for mastering a mountain or a hard exam. '이기다' is about the result of a match or fight, while '정복하다' carries the feeling of making the target completely yours.

en: present; give as a gift; offer as a freebie

examples.en: We give a souvenir to the guests who come to the event.

examples.ko: 이 책을 사면 예쁜 가방을 증정한대요.
examples.en: They say you get a pretty bag with this book.
The company gave gift certificates to the employees.

examples.ko: 이벤트에 참여하신 분께 쿠폰을 증정할 거예요.
examples.en: We will give a coupon to those who join the event.
It was a gift giveaway day, so the shop was crowded.

examples.ko: 졸업생에게 꽃다발을 증정하고 같이 사진도 찍었어요.
examples.en: We gave the graduate a bouquet and took photos together.

explain: 가게 광고나 행사 안내에서 자주 보이는 말이에요. 친구에게 줄 때는 '주다', 선물할 때는 '선물하다'를 쓰고, '증정하다'는 공식적인 자리나 광고 문구에 어울려요. 말할 때보다 글에서 더 자주 나와요.
explain_en: You often see this in shop ads and event notices. With friends you say '주다' or '선물하다'; '증정하다' fits formal occasions and advertising copy, and it appears more in writing than in speech.

examples.en: The students march around the field in line.
The soldiers marched in the wide square.
People sang while marching down the street.

examples.ko: 축제 퍼레이드가 시청 앞까지 행진할 거예요.
examples.en: The festival parade will march up to the city hall.
Children gathered to see the marching band.

examples.ko: 우리는 다 같이 행진하고 나서 점심을 먹었어요.
examples.en: After marching together, we had lunch.

explain: 여럿이 줄을 맞춰 걸을 때 써요. 그냥 걷는 '걷다'와 달리 박자나 목적이 있는 느낌이에요. 축제 퍼레이드, 군대, 운동회에서 자주 나와요. 혼자 걷는 일에는 거의 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: Use it when many people walk together in line. Unlike plain '걷다', it feels rhythmic or purposeful. It comes up at festival parades, in the military and at sports days, and is almost never used for one person walking alone.

examples.en: Under the microscope, the cell divides in two.
The team split in two because of different opinions.

examples.ko: 친구들이 두 편으로 분열하면 같이 놀기 어려워요.
examples.en: If friends split into two sides, it is hard to hang out together.

examples.ko: 작은 세포가 계속 분열하는 모습을 사진으로 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw in photos how a small cell keeps dividing.

examples.ko: 가족이 분열하지 않게 서로 이야기를 많이 해요.
examples.en: We talk a lot so that the family does not fall apart.
I am worried the group might split up.

explain: 세포가 나뉘는 과학 이야기와, 모임이나 팀이 갈라지는 이야기에 둘 다 써요. '갈라지다'는 틈이 생길 때도 쓰지만 '분열하다'는 하나였던 집단이나 세포가 나뉠 때 써요. 반대말은 '단결하다'예요.
explain_en: It works both for cells dividing in science and for a group or team breaking apart. '갈라지다' can also mean a crack appearing, but '분열하다' is for something that was one, such as a group or a cell, dividing. The opposite is '단결하다'.

en: commission; request (a professional to do a job)

examples.en: The company commissioned a designer to make a new logo.

examples.ko: 이 일은 전문가에게 의뢰하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It is better to hand this job to an expert.
I called the hospital to request a test.
I am looking for a place to order a translation.

examples.ko: 친구가 저에게 그림을 의뢰해서 열심히 그렸어요.
examples.en: A friend commissioned a painting from me, so I worked hard on it.

examples.ko: 수리를 의뢰하고 나서 사흘 뒤에 받았어요.
examples.en: I got it back three days after I requested the repair.

explain: 전문가나 전문 기관에 일을 맡길 때 써요. '부탁하다'는 가까운 사이에도 쓰지만 '의뢰하다'는 번역, 수리, 검사처럼 업무를 맡기는 느낌이에요. 명사 '의뢰'로 '의뢰가 들어오다'처럼도 써요.
explain_en: Use it when you hand a job to a professional or a specialized organization. '부탁하다' works between close people, but '의뢰하다' feels like handing over work such as translation, repairs or tests. The noun '의뢰' appears in phrases like '의뢰가 들어오다' (a request comes in).

examples.en: The army retreated because the enemy was strong.
The economy is declining as business gets worse.

examples.ko: 한 걸음 후퇴해서 다시 생각해 봐요.
examples.en: Let's step back and think again.

examples.ko: 복지 제도가 후퇴하지 않도록 사람들이 목소리를 냈어요.
examples.en: People spoke up so that the welfare system would not slide backward.
I practice every day for fear my skills will slip.

examples.ko: 공격하던 팀이 갑자기 후퇴하는 바람에 골을 먹었어요.
examples.en: The attacking team suddenly fell back and we conceded a goal.

explain: 싸움에서 뒤로 물러날 때 쓰고, 실력이나 경제가 나빠질 때 비유로도 써요. 반대말은 '전진하다'나 '발전하다'예요. 일상에서 그냥 뒤로 가는 건 '물러나다'나 '뒤로 가다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used when pulling back in a fight, and figuratively when skills or the economy get worse. The opposites are '전진하다' and '발전하다'. For simply moving back in daily life people say '물러나다' or '뒤로 가다'.

examples.en: The committee deliberates on the new rules.
The city hall reviewed the building plan.
They will deliberate on the budget at today's meeting.

examples.ko: 계획을 심의하는 데 한 달이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a month to review the plan.

examples.ko: 영화를 심의한 뒤에 관람 등급을 정해요.
examples.en: They set the age rating after reviewing the film.

examples.ko: 위원들이 의견을 나누며 천천히 심의하고 있어요.
examples.en: The members are slowly deliberating while sharing opinions.

explain: 공식 기관이나 위원회가 안건을 자세히 따져 볼 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 쓰고 뉴스나 공문에 나와요. '검토하다'는 누구나 쓰지만 '심의하다'는 정해진 기관이 판단하는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: Use it when an official body or committee examines a matter closely. It is rare in daily talk and shows up in the news and official papers. Anyone can '검토하다', but '심의하다' feels like a designated body making a judgment.

en: lose power; have a power outage; get cut off (electricity)

examples.en: The whole town lost power because of the storm.
The power suddenly went out and I could not see anything.
If the building loses power, the elevators stop.
While the power was out, we lit candles and talked.
I bought a flashlight in case the power goes out at night.

examples.ko: 어젯밤에 정전되었는데 한 시간 뒤에 들어왔어요.
examples.en: The power went out last night and came back an hour later.

explain: 전기가 갑자기 끊길 때 써요. 일상에서는 '정전이 되다', '불이 나가다'라고 더 많이 말해요. 전기가 다시 들어오면 '전기가 들어오다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Use it when electricity is suddenly cut. In daily speech people more often say '정전이 되다' or '불이 나가다'. When power returns, you say '전기가 들어오다'.

examples.ko: 학교에서 오늘 아침에 합격 결과를 통보했어요.
examples.en: The school notified us of the admission result this morning.
The company informs employees of the moving date.
It is a problem if they suddenly announce that the contract is over.
We will notify you of the exam result by email.
Telling people in a one-sided way is not good.

examples.ko: 병원에서 검사 결과를 통보하고 나서 약을 처방했어요.
examples.en: After giving the test result, the hospital prescribed medicine.

explain: 결정된 사실을 공식적으로 알려 줄 때 써요. '알려 주다'와 달리 상대 의견을 묻지 않고 결과만 전하는 느낌이 강해요. '일방적으로 통보하다'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: Use it to officially announce something already decided. Unlike '알려 주다', it strongly suggests passing on only the result without asking the other person's opinion. A common phrase is '일방적으로 통보하다' (to notify one-sidedly).

examples.en: The driver speeds up the car.
The train gradually picked up speed after leaving.

examples.ko: 일을 빨리 끝내려고 작업을 가속할 거예요.
examples.en: I will speed up the work to finish it quickly.

examples.ko: 새 기술이 경쟁을 가속하는 것 같아요.
examples.en: New technology seems to speed up competition.
The internet is accelerating social change.
The plane accelerated on the runway and rose into the sky.

explain: 속도나 움직임을 더 빠르게 할 때 써요. 자동차뿐 아니라 '경쟁', '개발'처럼 눈에 안 보이는 흐름에도 써요. '변화가 가속화되다', '가속화하다'처럼 '-화'를 붙인 형태도 아주 많이 보여요. 반대말은 '감속하다'예요. 일상 말로는 '속도를 올리다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Use it when making speed or movement faster. Besides cars, it also works for invisible trends such as competition and development. The form with 화, as in 변화가 가속화되다 and 가속화하다, is also very common. The opposite is 감속하다. In everyday speech 속도를 올리다 sounds more natural.

en: open (to traffic or service); be connected

examples.ko: 새 지하철 노선이 다음 달에 개통돼요.
examples.en: The new subway line opens next month.
Travel became easier because the highway opened.
Once my phone is activated, I will text you right away.

examples.ko: 다리가 개통된 날 많은 사람이 구경하러 왔어요.
examples.en: Many people came to look on the day the bridge opened.
The internet has not been connected yet.

examples.ko: 공항까지 가는 철도가 곧 개통될 거예요.
examples.en: The railway to the airport will open soon.

explain: 길, 지하철, 전화, 인터넷 같은 것을 처음으로 쓸 수 있게 될 때 써요. 새 휴대폰을 사고 번호를 쓸 수 있게 하는 것도 '개통하다'라고 해요. '열리다'는 문이나 행사에, '개통되다'는 길과 통신에 써요.
explain_en: Use it when a road, subway, phone line or internet becomes usable for the first time. Activating a new phone number is also '개통하다'. '열리다' is for doors and events, while '개통되다' is for roads and communication lines.

en: resolve; make up one's mind firmly

examples.en: I resolved to exercise every day this year.

examples.ko: 그는 다시는 지각하지 않겠다고 결의하고 일찍 잤어요.
examples.en: He vowed never to be late again and went to bed early.

examples.ko: 다 같이 결의하는 모습이 정말 멋있었어요.
examples.en: The way everyone made a resolution together looked really cool.

examples.ko: 주민들이 마을을 깨끗이 하기로 결의한 뒤 청소를 시작했어요.
examples.en: After the residents resolved to clean up the town, they started cleaning.

examples.ko: 시험에 붙기로 결의해서 매일 도서관에 가요.
examples.en: I am determined to pass the exam, so I go to the library every day.

examples.ko: 다음에는 꼭 이기자고 다 같이 결의할 거예요.
examples.en: We will all resolve together to win next time.

explain: 마음을 굳게 먹거나 여럿이 함께 공식적으로 정할 때 써요. '결심하다'는 혼자 마음먹을 때 자주 쓰고, '결의하다'는 더 단단하고 단체가 함께하는 느낌이 있어요. 일상 대화에서는 '결심하다'가 훨씬 흔해요.
explain_en: Use it when you firmly set your mind or when a group formally decides together. '결심하다' is common for deciding alone, while '결의하다' feels firmer and more collective. In daily conversation '결심하다' is far more common.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 말과 행동이 자주 모순돼요.
examples.en: His words and actions often contradict each other.

examples.ko: 두 사람의 설명이 서로 모순되어서 이상했어요.
examples.en: The two accounts contradicted each other, which was strange.

examples.ko: 모순되는 내용이 한 글에 같이 들어 있어요.
examples.en: Contradictory content is in the same text.

examples.ko: 결과가 처음 계획과 모순되지 않아서 다행이에요.
examples.en: I am glad the result does not conflict with the original plan.

examples.ko: 건강을 챙기면서 밤을 새우는 건 모순된 행동이에요.
examples.en: Looking after your health while staying up all night is contradictory behavior.

examples.ko: 앞뒤가 모순될 때는 다시 확인해 봐요.
examples.en: When the beginning and the end contradict each other, check again.

explain: 말, 생각, 행동이 서로 맞지 않을 때 써요. '모순이 있다', '모순이 생기다'처럼 명사 '모순'도 많이 써요. 따로 보면 맞아 보이는데 같이 놓으면 안 맞는다는 느낌이고, '앞뒤가 안 맞다'로 바꿔 말할 수 있어요.
explain_en: Use it when words, thoughts or actions do not fit each other. The noun '모순' is also common, as in '모순이 있다' or '모순이 생기다'. Each part may seem right alone but they clash together, and you can say '앞뒤가 안 맞다' instead.

examples.en: That empty house has been left unattended for a long time.
A bicycle had been left by the roadside.
A neglected building can be dangerous.
If a wound is neglected, it gets worse.
The puppy that had been neglected met a new family.

examples.ko: 공원에 쓰레기가 방치되지 않도록 매일 치워요.
examples.en: We clean every day so trash is not left in the park.

explain: 돌봐 주는 사람이 없어서 그냥 놓여 있는 상태를 말할 때 써요. '방치하다'와 달리 놓인 물건이나 사람이 주인공이에요. '버려지다'처럼 완전히 버린 건 아니지만 아무도 신경 쓰지 않았다는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: Use it for a state of being left as is because no one looks after it. Unlike '방치하다', the thing or person left behind is the subject. It is not fully abandoned like '버려지다', but it feels like nobody paid attention.

examples.en: You must not leave trash lying in the street.

examples.ko: 부모가 아이를 방치하는 일은 없어야 해요.
examples.en: Parents must never neglect their children.
I left a small problem alone and it grew big.

examples.ko: 고장 난 자전거를 오래 방치해서 녹이 슬었어요.
examples.en: The broken bike was left for so long that it rusted.
Don't ignore it; go to the hospital right away.

examples.ko: 집을 방치할 수는 없어서 한 달에 한 번 청소해요.
examples.en: I cannot leave the house uncared for, so I clean it once a month.

explain: 해야 할 일을 하지 않고 그냥 놓아둘 때 써요. '내버려 두다'와 비슷한데 '방치하다'는 돌봐야 할 사람이 돌보지 않는다는 나쁜 느낌이 있어요. 그래서 쓰레기, 건물, 병, 아이처럼 돌봐야 하는 대상에 많이 써요.
explain_en: Use it when you leave something as it is instead of doing what you should. It is close to '내버려 두다', but '방치하다' carries a negative feeling that the person responsible is not caring for it. So it is common with trash, buildings, illness and children.

examples.en: The teacher hands out snacks to the students.
We divided the work fairly, so everyone felt at ease.
We first decided how to share the profit.
I will assign roles to the team members.

examples.ko: 돈을 분배하고 나서 서로 싸우지 않았어요.
examples.en: They did not fight after splitting the money.
While dividing the food, I found one was missing.

explain: 정해진 몫이나 규칙에 따라 나누어 줄 때 써요. '나누다'는 반으로 자르는 것도 되지만 '분배하다'는 사람마다 몫을 정해 준다는 느낌이에요. 일, 돈, 역할 같은 말과 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: Use it when handing out portions according to a set share or rule. '나누다' can mean just cutting in half, but '분배하다' feels like deciding each person's share. It pairs well with work, money and roles.

examples.en: Wealthy countries give aid to poor countries.
They sent food aid to the country hit by the earthquake.

examples.ko: 정부가 피해 지역에 쌀을 원조해 줬어요.
examples.en: The government sent rice aid to the disaster area.

examples.ko: 학교를 짓는 데 필요한 돈을 원조하는 단체예요.
examples.en: It is an organization that funds what is needed to build schools.
Even if I want to help, our situation is hard.

examples.ko: 도움이 필요한 사람들을 원조할 방법을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: We are looking for a way to give aid to people in need.

explain: 나라나 단체가 어려운 곳에 돈, 음식, 물건을 보내 줄 때 써요. 친구를 도울 때는 '돕다'를 쓰고, '원조하다'는 규모가 크고 공식적인 도움에 써요. 뉴스에서 '경제 원조', '원조 물자'처럼 나와요.
explain_en: Use it when a country or organization sends money, food or goods to a place in need. Between friends you say '돕다'; '원조하다' is for large, official help. In the news you see '경제 원조' and '원조 물자'.

en: leave; deviate from; break away from

examples.en: The train went off the track.

examples.ko: 선수 한 명이 대열에서 이탈한 걸 아무도 몰랐어요.
examples.en: Nobody noticed that one player had dropped out of the line.
Leaving the path is dangerous, so follow the signs.

examples.ko: 비행기가 정해진 경로를 이탈하는 일은 드물어요.
examples.en: It is rare for a plane to leave its set route.
Customers keep leaving, so the company is worried.
I check every day so I don't stray from the plan.

explain: 정해진 길, 줄, 집단, 규칙에서 벗어나 떨어져 나갈 때 써요. 기차는 선로를, 선수는 대열을, 고객은 서비스를 이탈해요. '벗어나다'보다 딱딱하고 뉴스나 업무에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: Use it when something leaves a set path, line, group or rule. A train leaves its track, a player leaves the formation, a customer leaves a service. It is stiffer than '벗어나다' and common in news and business.

examples.ko: 짐 무게가 초과돼서 추가 요금을 냈어요.
examples.en: The baggage was overweight, so I paid an extra fee.
We must be careful not to go over budget.

examples.ko: 정원이 초과되어서 더 탈 수 없어요.
examples.en: The capacity has been exceeded, so no more can get on.
If the time limit is exceeded, points are deducted.

examples.ko: 한도가 초과된 카드는 쓸 수 없어요.
examples.en: A card that is over its limit cannot be used.

examples.ko: 인원이 초과될 것 같아서 일찍 신청했어요.
examples.en: The number of people looked likely to go over, so I applied early.

explain: 정해진 수나 양, 시간을 넘었을 때 써요. 반대말은 '미달되다'예요. '넘다'보다 딱딱해서 안내문과 규칙에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Use it when a set number, amount or time is passed. The opposite is '미달되다'. It is stiffer than '넘다' and often appears in notices and rules.
